name: alloc_hugepages
synopsis: void *syscall(SYS_alloc_hugepages, int key, void addr[.len], size_t len, int prot, int flag);
description: alloc_hugepages allocates huge pages in memory for the process, which are larger than standard pages and not subject to swapping. It supports shared or private memory segments based on a key identifier.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Identifier for the pages; 0 for private, positive for shared and inherited by child processes.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Hint for the address, which the kernel may ignore; for free_hugepages, it specifies the address to free.

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length of the required segment, must be a multiple of the huge page size.

parameters.name: prot
parameters.description: Memory protection flags, such as PROT_READ, PROT_WRITE, or PROT_EXEC.

parameters.name: flag
parameters.description: Flags; if key is positive, IPC_CREAT creates a new segment if none exists.

return_value.success: Returns the allocated virtual address for alloc_hugepages, or 0 for free_hugepages
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, errno is set

errors.description: The system call is not supported on this kernel.
No segment with the given key exists and IPC_CREAT is not set.

bugs: These system calls were removed in Linux 2.5.54 and are not available in modern kernels; use hugetlbfs filesystem instead.
